text: This is what the LORD says: Keep justice and do what is right, for my salvation is close at hand and my righteousness is about to be revealed.

versions.text: This is what the LORD says: Guard justice and do what is right, for my salvation is close at hand and my righteousness is about to be revealed.
versions.explanation: "Guard justice" is a somewhat wooden rendering of שִׁמְרוּ מִשְׁפָּט; "Keep justice" (or "Maintain justice") reads more naturally aloud while preserving the same verb that recurs in vv. 2, 4, 6 ("keeps the Sabbath").

text: Blessed is the one who does this, the man who holds fast to it — who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.
Let no foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, "The LORD will surely exclude me from his people." And let no eunuch say, "I am nothing but a withered tree."
For this is what the LORD says: To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, who choose what pleases me and hold fast to my covenant —
to them I will give, within my house and within my walls, a memorial and a name better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will never be cut off.

versions.text: to them I will give, within my house and within my walls, a monument and a name better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will never be cut off.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew idiom yad va-shem denotes a lasting memorial; "memorial" is a slightly more accurate and idiomatic rendering than "monument," which suggests a physical structure only. Consider a footnote: "Hebrew yad va-shem, literally 'a hand and a name.'"

text: And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to serve him, to love the name of the LORD and to be his servants — all who keep the Sabbath without profaning it and hold fast to my covenant —

these I will bring to my holy mountain and give them joy in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
So declares the Lord GOD, who gathers the outcasts of Israel: I will gather still others to him, besides those already gathered to him.

versions.text: So declares the Lord GOD, who gathers the outcasts of Israel: I will gather still others to him, besides those already gathered.
versions.explanation: Minor clarification: the Hebrew repeats the pronominal reference ("to him, to those gathered of his"), and the added "to him" closes the sentence with better oral cadence.

text: All you beasts of the field, come and devour — all you beasts of the forest!
Israel's watchmen are blind, every one of them; they know nothing. They are all mute dogs that cannot bark, dreaming as they lie there, in love with sleep.
They are greedy dogs that never have enough. And they are shepherds who understand nothing; every one of them has turned to his own way, each seeking his own gain, to the last of them.
"Come," they say, "let me get some wine; let us drink our fill of strong drink! And tomorrow will be like today — even better, far grander!"

versions.text: "Come," they say, "let me fetch wine; let us drink our fill of strong drink! And tomorrow will be like today — even better, far grander!"
versions.explanation: "Fetch" is archaic and slightly stilted for oral reading; "get some wine" preserves the sense of אֶקְחָה־יַיִן while flowing better in speech.
